_comment: Storage macOS fills by itself (AGENTS.md rule 6: patterns are data). Research and sources: docs/STORAGE-RESEARCH-PLAN.md section 2. Paths: '~' is the home folder; a trailing '*' in the last component matches by prefix. action: never = macOS manages it, nothing to do; guide = free it through macOS's own settings (steps); trash = may be added to Cleanup. settingsPane: a System Settings extension id, checked against /System/Library/ExtensionKit/Extensions on macOS 26.5.

entries.title: Apple Intelligence & Siri models
entries.why: On-device models for Apple Intelligence, Siri and translation. macOS downloads them and protects them; no app can delete them.
steps: Open System Settings › Apple Intelligence & Siri.
Turn off what you don't use. macOS removes those models later by itself.

entries.title: Language, dictation & voices
entries.why: Spelling, prediction, dictation and spoken-content voices for the languages you use. Protected by macOS.
steps: Remove languages you don't type in: System Settings › Keyboard › Text Input.
Remove extra voices: System Settings › Accessibility › Spoken Content › System Voice › Manage Voices.

entries.title: Downloaded macOS updates
entries.why: Updates macOS has downloaded but not installed yet. Deleting them by hand can break the next update.
steps: Install the waiting update in System Settings › General › Software Update. macOS clears the download afterwards.

entries.title: Aerial wallpaper & screen saver videos
entries.why: The moving landscape videos behind aerial wallpapers and screen savers, often hundreds of MB each.
steps: Choose a still wallpaper and a non-aerial screen saver in System Settings › Wallpaper.
macOS downloads aerials again if you pick one later.

entries.title: Wallpaper cache
entries.why: A cache the wallpaper agent keeps. A known macOS bug can let it grow very large; Apple calls deleting it by hand risky and unsupported.
steps: There is no supported way to clear it, so freedisk.space leaves it alone.
If it keeps growing, report it to Apple with Feedback Assistant.

entries.title: macOS installer apps
entries.why: Full macOS installers, often over 12 GB each. Once macOS is installed you don't need them; you can download them again from the App Store.
steps: Add them to Cleanup. They go to the Trash first.

entries.title: System logs
entries.why: macOS's unified log. It caps its own size and removes old entries; deleting it breaks diagnostics.
steps: Nothing to do: macOS keeps this in check.
